short_summary: Create a virtual machine and its supporting network resources.
long_summary: Provision an Azure virtual machine in the specified resource group along with the supporting virtual network, subnet, network security group, network interface, and public IP address in a single orchestrated call. The VM size, administrator credentials, and target location must all be provided. Resource names supplied for `--virtual-network-name` and `--network-interface-name` are created if they do not already exist in the resource group. By default a network security group named `{vm}NSG` is created, or updated if it already exists. A network security group the command creates has one inbound rule for the image's operating system, allowing traffic from any source: `rdp` (TCP port 3389) for Windows or `default-allow-ssh` (TCP port 22) for Linux. Pass `--nsg` a name to reuse the network security group of that name, unchanged, when it exists and create it when it does not, a resource ID to attach an existing network security group, or `""` to create none. By default a Standard, static public IP address named `{vm}PublicIP` is created, or updated if it already exists. Pass `--public-ip-address` a name to reuse the public IP address of that name when it exists and create it when it does not, a resource ID to attach an existing public IP address, or `""` to create none. Use `--zone` to place the virtual machine in a single availability zone. Use `--storage-sku` to choose the storage SKU of the managed OS disk, such as `Premium_LRS`, `StandardSSD_LRS`, `Standard_LRS`, `Premium_ZRS`, or `StandardSSD_ZRS`; when omitted, the service default applies. Pass `--tags` to tag the virtual machine and every network resource the command creates; resources the command only attaches keep their own tags, such as network interfaces passed to `--nics`, the virtual network of an existing subnet selected with `--subnet`, or an existing network security group or public IP address. The command returns the new virtual machine with the power state and the public and private IP addresses that `az vm show -d` reports.

short_summary: Deallocate a virtual machine and release its compute resources.
long_summary: Shut down a virtual machine and release its compute resources, so you are no longer billed for compute. Use `az vm stop` instead to power the machine off while keeping it allocated. Target a single VM with `--name` and `--resource-group`, or pass one or more full resource IDs to `--ids` to deallocate several VMs in one invocation. When `--ids` is used it supplies the subscription, resource group, and VM name for each target, so `--name`, `--resource-group`, and `--subscription-id` are ignored. Pass `--hibernate` to preserve the machine's memory state, or `--force-deallocate` to force the operation. The command waits for the long-running operation to finish and returns no output on success.

short_summary: Power off (stop) a running virtual machine.
long_summary: Power off a running virtual machine while leaving its compute resources allocated. The virtual machine continues to be billed; use `az vm deallocate` to release the compute resources and stop compute charges. Target a single VM with `--name` and `--resource-group`, or pass one or more full resource IDs to `--ids` to power off several VMs in one invocation. When `--ids` is used it supplies the subscription, resource group, and VM name for each target, so `--name`, `--resource-group`, and `--subscription-id` are ignored. Pass `--skip-shutdown` to power the machine off immediately instead of requesting a graceful guest shutdown. The command waits for the long-running operation to finish and returns no output on success.
